reception: Its citations are few and sit at the edges of their papers, coming from the sparse-compilation community the TACO line addresses. The structured-tensor-algebra work of Ghorbani, Bauer, and Grosser engages it most directly, discussing the node-schema approach while compressing structured tensors; WingSpan, Bonsai, and work on optimizing sparse tensor compilation for sparse output cite it as an instance of what format-general compilers cover; a paper on exploiting sparsity in convolutional networks on GPUs cites a finding as evidence. None of the judged citations builds on the system itself, so the paper functions as a boundary marker — cited to note that mutable, pointer-based sparse structures are within a compiler's reach. The implementation lives in the tensor-compiler/taco repository, and an evaluated artifact accompanies the paper.
